title: He didn’t just wear a coat.
paragraphs:
He didn’t just wear a coat.
He wore a target.
And maybe… so do you.
You thought it was just about Joseph.

A colorful robe.
A jealous family.
A dramatic fall.

But if you look closer—
this story is staring back at you.
Because some of you aren’t just wearing favor…
You’re hiding it.

Or worse—
you’re ashamed of it.
Let’s open the wound.

Joseph didn’t do anything immoral.
He didn’t steal.
He didn’t cheat.
He was simply loved differently.
And that alone made him a problem.

Genesis 37:3 (NIV)
“Now Israel loved Joseph more than any of his other sons… and he made him a richly ornamented robe.”
That robe?

It wasn’t just colorful.
It was loud.

Visible.
Unavoidable.
Provoking.

Some scholars interpret the phrase “richly ornamented robe” (Hebrew: ketonet passim) as a long-sleeved garment worn by royalty—
not by laborers.
Meaning Joseph wasn’t dressed for the field…
He was dressed for destiny.
And that’s where the tension begins.

Because when God marks you—
people notice.
And not everyone celebrates what God is doing in you.
Let’s be honest.
You’ve felt it.

The side-eyes.
The subtle distance.
The tension you can’t explain.

You didn’t change…
but somehow everything changed.
Here’s the hard truth:
Favor will expose what people try to hide.

Their insecurity.
Their comparison.
Their silent resentment.
Joseph’s brothers didn’t hate the fabric.
They hated the implication.
And maybe that’s you right now.

You feel guilty for being blessed.
You shrink your voice.
You downplay your calling.

Because deep inside…
you don’t want to be rejected.
So you bury your coat.

You fold it.
Hide it.
Pretend it’s not there.
But hiding your calling doesn’t protect you.
It slowly erases you.
Joseph wore the coat.
And it cost him.

Genesis 37:4 (NIV)
“When his brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him…”
Hated him.

Not ignored.
Not misunderstood.
Hated.
And hatred escalated.

Mocking.
Plotting.
Betrayal.
Then came the pit.
Let that sink in.
The coat didn’t lead to applause.
It led to a hole in the ground.
And some of you are there right now.

In a pit you didn’t plan.
A season you didn’t deserve.
A silence you don’t understand.
Here’s the whisper of shame:

“Maybe I should’ve stayed small.”
“Maybe I shouldn’t have stood out.”
“Maybe I deserved this.”
No.
Listen carefully.
The pit is not proof you were wrong.
It’s often proof you were chosen.
Because God will never waste what He anoints.
But here’s where it gets deeper.
Joseph was stripped of his robe.

Genesis 37:23 (NIV)
“So when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped him of his robe—the ornate robe he was wearing.”
Stripped.

Publicly.
Violently.
Intentionally.
That moment?
That’s where shame tries to rewrite your identity.
“Without the coat… who are you now?”
And that’s the question many are living in.

Without the platform…
Without the recognition…
Without the visible blessing…
Who are you?
Now watch this.
They took the coat—
but they couldn’t take the calling.
Because what God places on you can be removed.
But what He places in you?
Untouchable.
Years passed.

Slavery.
False accusations.
Prison.
Joseph’s life looked like failure.
But heaven was writing something else.

Genesis 50:20 (NIV)
“You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good…”
There it is.
The divine reversal.

What looked like rejection
was actually redirection.

What felt like abandonment
was divine positioning.
Now let’s go to the cross.
Because Joseph’s story whispers a louder name.
Jesus.

Like Joseph—
He was loved by the Father.

Matthew 3:17 (NIV)
“This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased.”

Like Joseph—
He was hated without cause.

John 15:25 (NIV)
“They hated me without reason.”

Like Joseph—
He was stripped.

Matthew 27:28 (NIV)
“They stripped him and put a scarlet robe on him…”
But here’s where it explodes into glory.
Joseph was stripped of a robe of favor.
Jesus was stripped so you could be clothed in righteousness.

2 Corinthians 5:21 (NIV)
“God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.”
This is the Gospel.

Not self-improvement.
Not behavior modification.
Substitution.
Redemption.
Grace.
Your shame doesn’t get the final word.
Jesus does.
You don’t have to hide anymore.

Not your past.
Not your calling.
Not your wounds.
Because in Christ—
you are covered.
Not with a temporary coat…
but with eternal grace.
So what do you do now?
Stop shrinking.
Stop apologizing for what God is doing in your life.
Stop letting the fear of rejection silence your obedience.
Bring your shame to Jesus.

Bring your hidden guilt.
Your fear.
Your insecurity.
And let Him clothe you again.
Not in pride.
But in purpose.
Not in performance.
But in identity.
Right now—this moment—
He’s inviting you.
Not to perform.
Not to impress.
But to surrender.
Say it with your heart:
“Jesus, I’m done hiding.”
